title: Let The Wick Form, Trade The Body (Stop Getting Stopped Out)
description: Learn how protected swings, CISD, higher timeframe candles, and fractal entries help confirm when a wick has formed before trading expansion.

body.text: Introduction
Every expansion candle has a wick before it has a body. The mistake is trying to trade the body before the wick has actually formed.

The logic is simple: if a higher timeframe candle is expected to expand in one direction, there needs to be evidence that its wick has formed first. Once that wick has formed, the focus shifts to getting on side with the body and the expansion that follows.
Understand the Protected Swing
A protected swing forms when price reaches an important level and then closes through the series of candles into that level.
That important level can be a high, low, or fair value gap. The close through that series of candles is what confirms the shift. The sweep itself is not the confirmation.
This is the same change in the state of delivery used to confirm swing formations, but here the logic is applied inside the continuation candle to determine when its wick has formed.
Let the Wick Form First
If a higher timeframe candle is expected to expand higher, there is no reason to immediately buy when that candle opens.
The candle could still trade lower and form its wick before expanding higher.
So the question is simple:
Has this higher timeframe candle formed its wick yet?
If the answer is no, there is no protected swing to trust as the low. Entering too early can mean getting stopped out while the market is still forming the wick.
Once price creates the short-term bearish movement and then shifts back bullish, the low can be anticipated as formed. That gives a level to trade away from.
Use the Intra-Candle Change in the State of Delivery
This is where the intra-candle change in the state of delivery becomes useful.

Price reaches an important level, such as a fair value gap, and then closes through the series of candles that created the move into it. That creates a new protected swing inside the higher timeframe candle.
Now there is a logical level that should hold if the higher timeframe candle is going to expand in the expected direction.
For a bullish candle:
Bearish movement → important level → bullish change in the state of delivery → protected swing → expansion higher
For a bearish candle, the same logic happens in reverse.
Trade the Body, Not the Wick
Once the wick has formed, the opportunity changes.
There is no longer a need to predict where the wick will form. There is now a level that can be used as the invalidation, along with an expectation for the candle to expand away from it.
This is why entering around the opening price of the higher timeframe candle can make sense when the setup allows for it.
Let the wick form, then trade the body.

If the candle is truly an expansion candle, the body is where the move happens. Getting on side early allows participation in that expansion instead of chasing it after the move has already developed.
Confirm It on the Lower Timeframe
The entry does not always need to come directly from the higher timeframe.
Once the higher timeframe wick is anticipated to have formed, drop to a lower timeframe fractal model and look for its own confirmation.
That could be:
- An intra-candle change in the state of delivery
- A new protected swing
- A lower timeframe fractal setup for a more precise entry
The higher timeframe provides the expectation. The lower timeframe can provide the execution.
Place the Stop on the Wick
Once a protected swing has formed, the stop has a logical location.
If the expectation is bullish, the protected swing becomes the low that should hold. If the expectation is bearish, the protected swing becomes the high that should hold.
If the wick has actually formed, that level should hold while the candle expands away from it.
If price takes that protected swing, the assumption that the wick has formed is wrong, and the trade is invalidated.
Know What the Candle Is Reaching For
The wick does not form in isolation.

There still needs to be an understanding of where the higher timeframe candle is expected to expand toward. Look at the surrounding structure, fair value gaps, swing points, and higher timeframe liquidity.
Once the wick has formed, the body can be traded toward those objectives.
This gives the setup more structure than simply seeing a protected swing and entering. The higher timeframe expectation, wick formation, confirmation, invalidation, and target all work together.
The Logic Is Fractal
This can be used on any timeframe because the logic does not change.
A daily candle can form its wick and expand. An hourly candle can do the same thing. A 15-minute candle can do the same thing.
The timeframe changes, but the question stays the same:
Has the wick formed yet?
If not, wait.
If yes, look for the entry and trade the body.
That is the logic behind letting the wick form before trading the expansion.
Final Thoughts
When looking for an entry, the goal is not to take a random trade inside a higher timeframe candle.
The wick needs to form first. A protected swing or intra-candle change in the state of delivery provides a way to mechanically define that.
Once the wick can be trusted, the focus shifts to trading the body, placing the stop on the invalidation, and letting the expansion work toward its objective.
Let the wick form. Trade the body.
